releases.name: v1.4.0
releases.body:
## v1.4.0 — 2026-07-01

## New Features

### Discovery Logs

-   A new section under the Discovery dropdown for inspecting the results of a specific discovery schedule run end-to-end. Data is populated by the new extract_discovery_logs.py sync script and rendered in a single page with four areas:
-   Run overview — MID Server live record (name, IP, version, validation status, pool) and discovery schedule details (run time, IP ranges, discovery type) presented as side-by-side info cards.
-   Run summary — the latest completed run for the configured schedule: run number, state badge, start/end timestamps, and four stat boxes for Started, Completed, Progress, and Discover counts pulled from discovery_status.
-   Discovered CIs — every CI found during the run, grouped by class and rendered as expandable cards showing base attributes (install status, last discovered, serial number, manufacturer), class-specific details (OS, RAM, CPU, disk, version, MAC address, and other fields resolved from the actual CI table), and CMDB relations (type, direction, and linked CI name). A filter bar at the top lets you narrow to a specific CI type; clicking the active chip resets to All.
-   Discovery Log Messages — the full discovery_log record set for the run in a collapsible panel. A text search box filters by message content, source IP, or log level in real time, with a live X / total counter. Raw HTML tags in log messages are stripped before display.

 ## New sync script: extract_discovery_logs.py

  ### Connects to your ServiceNow instance and pulls:
  - MID Server record from ecc_agent
  - Discovery schedule and IP ranges from discovery_schedule + discovery_range_item
  - Latest completed run from discovery_status (filters out Running, Cancelled, Error, and Stopped states; fetches the last 10 by sys_created_on and picks the first completed one)
  - Log messages from discovery_log for that run
- Discovered CIs by extracting unique source IPs from discovery_log.source, resolving each IP against cmdb_ci, then querying the class-specific table (cmdb_ci_linux_server, cmdb_ci_app_server_tomcat, etc.) for extended fields and cmdb_rel_ci for relations

Output is written to backend/scripts/data/discovery_runs.json. Global variables MID_SERVER_NAME and DISCOVERY_SCHEDULE_NAME at the top of the script control which MID and schedule are targeted.

### AI Assistant — Discovery coverage

The RAG pipeline now indexes discovery run data alongside the existing Discovery and CMDB corpora. On every backend startup the run summary and each discovered CI are flattened into searchable documents and indexed with BM25 + sentence-transformers. The following query types are now answered directly from synced data:

- Run inventory: "what was discovered in the latest run?" — the summary document carries a per-class CI count breakdown so the AI can enumerate all types found
- Hardware attributes: "how much RAM does webservices-infra have?", "what OS is docker-infra running?"
- Software and middleware: "any MongoDB instances?", "what version of NGINX is deployed?"
- Container infrastructure: "what Docker containers are running?", "what images are in the registry?"
- Specific CI lookup: "what is installed on docker-infra?", "what are the relations of Tomcat@webservices-infra?"

Trigger coverage uses two complementary mechanisms: a _DISCO_RUN_KWORDS frozenset covering hardware terms (ram, cpu, disk), middleware (nginx, apache, tomcat, mongodb, mysql), container terms (docker, container, image, infra), and generic Q&A words (what, which, list, any); plus a dynamic _disco_run_ci_toks set built at load time from every discovered CI name and FQDN, so a query mentioning a specific hostname triggers the discovery block even when no generic keyword matches.

## Bug Fixes

### CI filter chips showed raw class names
The CI_TABLE_LABEL map used incorrect ServiceNow class names for several types (cmdb_ci_web_server_apache instead of cmdb_ci_apache_web_server, cmdb_ci_nginx instead of cmdb_ci_nginx_web_server, cmdb_ci_db_mysql instead of cmdb_ci_db_mysql_instance). Filters for those types fell back to the raw cmdb_ci_* string. All entries have been corrected and the map extended to cover Docker Engine, Docker Container, Docker Image, Container Registry, Container Image, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, DNS Name, Disk Partition, File System, Router Interface (dscy_router_interface), Config File, and Printer.

### Unknown CI types always rendered in grey
Any CI class not explicitly listed in CI_TABLE_LABEL fell back to the raw table name, and any class not in CI_TABLE_COLOR fell back to slate grey (#94A3B8). Two helper functions — ciTableLabel() and ciTableColor() — now handle all lookups. For unknown types, ciTableLabel strips the cmdb_ci_ or dscy_ prefix, replaces underscores with spaces, and title-cases the result; ciTableColor returns a neutral slate default. Future CI types discovered by new patterns will render a readable label and a consistent colour without any code changes.

### RAG missed hardware and CI-specific attribute queries
classDetails values were indexed without their field names, so BM25 had no way to match a query for "RAM" against a document containing 2048. Field names are now included in the document body alongside values (ram 2048, cpu_count 4, etc.). The Network Adapter filter colour was also updated from slate grey to indigo to distinguish it from the fallback default.

releases.name: v1.3.0
releases.body:
## v1.3.0 — 2026-06-28

### New Features

#### CMDB Explorer
A new top-level module for browsing the CMDB configuration extracted from your ServiceNow instance. Data is populated by the new extract_cmdb_classes.py sync script and exposed through four sub-tabs:

-   CI Classes: every cmdb_ci_* table with name, label, parent class, scope, field count, and flags (Principal, IRE-linked, Extendable). Live search filters by name or label.

-   Identifiers: IRE identification rules from cmdb_identifier / cmdb_identifier_entry. Each identifier is expandable to show its ordered entries with criterion attributes, main attributes, priority, and matching flags (Fallback, Null OK, Exact count).

-   Relation Types    — the full cmdb_rel_type catalog with parent-to-child and child-to-parent descriptors.

-   Reconciliation    — cmdb_reconciliation_definition records per data source and CI class, including governed attributes, null-update fields, priority, and  active status.

#### AI Assistant — CMDB coverage
The RAG pipeline now indexes all four CMDB entity types using the same hybrid BM25 + semantic search used for Discovery data. Questions about CI class hierarchy, identification rules, relation types, and reconciliation configuration are answered directly from your synced instance data. The system prompt has been updated to reflect this coverage.

#### New sync script: extract_cmdb_classes.py
Connects to your ServiceNow instance and pulls sys_db_object, sys_dictionary, cmdb_class_info, cmdb_identifier,
cmdb_identifier_entry, cmdb_rel_type, and cmdb_reconciliation_definition into a single self-contained JSON file. Supports --no-fields to skip the field inventory for a faster run. Output defaults to backend/scripts/data/cmdb_classes.json.


### UI Redesign

#### Font stack
Switched from the system monospace stack to IBM Plex Sans (body and UI text) paired with IBM Plex Mono (code chips, inline code, and pre blocks). The new stack reads cleanly at the 13–13.5 px sizes used throughout the application.

#### Color palette
All muted text, border, and dark background tokens have been updated across every page and the ChatPanel to a higher-contrast green scale. Key changes: muted text lifted from #8EA898 to #506458 (light) and from #6A9880 to #4A6858 (dark), meeting WCAG AA contrast ratios at the sizes used. Body text, table header contrast, and card divider colors were adjusted in the same pass.

#### Visual details
Text selection highlight changed from the browser default (red on some platforms) to a green-tinted overlay that keeps selected text readable. Page headers now use a subtle directional gradient. Card border-radius increased to 12 px. Category icons on the Overview page replaced with inline SVG components — the Unicode cloud glyph (☁) does not render in IBM Plex.


### Bug Fixes

#### MID Server page subtitle truncated
The page subtitle was slicing the MID Server description at 120 characters and appending an ellipsis, cutting sentences mid-word. The truncation has been removed; the full name is now displayed.

#### "Principal only" CI class filter always empty
The filter relied on the principalClass field from cmdb_class_info, which is not populated on PDI instances — every class returned False, so the filter produced no results. The filter toggle has been removed entirely.

#### Duplicate item counters in CMDB sub-tabs
Each sub-tab card header showed a count that was already visible on the tab button above it. The redundant counters have been removed from the card headers.

#### ChatPanel colors and font not updated
The global color replacement pass in the previous release only targeted frontend/src/modules/. ChatPanel.jsx lives in frontend/src/components/ and was missed — it retained old muted color values and hardcoded font-mono on the two API key inputs and the markdown code/pre renderers. All values have been brought in line with the rest of the application.


### Documentation

#### README updated to cover:

-   CMDB Explorer section describing all four sub-tabs, their source tables, search behaviour, and AI assistant integration
-   extract_cmdb_classes.py usage examples and full options reference
-   Prerequisites note expanded with the seven CMDB tables required
-   Project structure tree updated to show the new cmdb/ module layout
-   AI Assistant section updated to reflect CMDB data coverage

releases.name: v1.2.0
releases.body:
## v1.2.0 — 2026-06-05

### Bug Fixes

#### AI Assistant crashed on credential-related questions

The `_prose_credential` function in `chat.py` was missing its `def` declaration — the function body was present but orphaned at module scope, so Python raised `NameError: name '_prose_credential' is not defined` whenever the RAG pipeline retrieved credential context and tried to format it. Any question touching credential types (e.g. *"What permissions does the Windows credential need?"*) caused the assistant to error out entirely. The `def _prose_credential(ct: dict) -> str:` line has been restored.

---

### Documentation

#### README updated

The README now fully covers the Discovery Credentials and MID Server sections that were introduced in v1.1.0:

- Intro sentence updated to mention both sections
- Table of contents expanded with entries for Discovery Credentials and MID Server
- Project structure tree updated to show `credentials.json`, `mid_server.json`, and all page components
- New **Discovery Credentials** section describing the credential type browser, detail panel contents, and AI assistant integration
- New **MID Server** section describing all 10 reference tabs and AI assistant integration
- AI Assistant section updated to reflect that the RAG pipeline now covers credentials and MID Server in addition to patterns and classifiers

---

## v1.1.0 — 2026-06-05                                                                                                          
   
  ### New Sections                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                  
  #### Discovery Credentials                                                                                                                        

  A dedicated page covering all 15 ServiceNow Discovery credential types — SSH Password, SSH Private Key, Windows/WMI, SNMP v1/v2c/v3, VMware, Basic
   Auth, AWS, Azure, GCP, JMX, JDBC, API Key, and External Credential Store.
                                                                                                                                                    
  - Type selector grid with badge-coded cards                                                                                                       
  - Per-type detail panel: configuration fields table, required permissions, CI table types, and usage notes
  - Overview strip explaining credential flow, Credential Affinity, and best practices                                                              
  - Fully indexed in the RAG pipeline (BM25 + semantic) — the AI Assistant now answers questions about credential types, required fields, and     
  privilege escalation                                                                                                                              
   
  #### MID Server                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                  
  A comprehensive reference page for the Management, Instrumentation, and Discovery Server, organised into 10 navigable sections.

  | Section | Content |
  |---|---|
  | Overview | ECC Queue communication model, key facts |
  | Capabilities | How each ITOM module uses the MID Server (Discovery, Service Mapping, Event Management, Orchestration, ITOM Health,              
  IntegrationHub) |
  | Requirements | Supported OS platforms, hardware sizing guidance, bundled JRE notes |                                                            
  | Network & Ports | Outbound-only model, per-port table for all Discovery probe protocols, proxy support |                                        
  | Security | TLS model, instance service account requirements, credential storage, OS account best practices |
  | Configuration | Full `config.xml` parameter reference with required/optional flags and defaults |                                               
  | MID States | Up, Down, Upgrading, Testing, Stopped, Purged — with visual state cards |                                                          
  | Clustering | Affinity rules, MID Server pools, HA behaviour |
  | Lifecycle | Installation steps, auto-upgrade process, validation procedure |                                                                    
  | Troubleshooting | Six common failure scenarios each with causes and step-by-step resolution |                                                   
   
  Fully indexed in the RAG pipeline across ~22 searchable section documents.                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                  
  ---

  ### Improvements

  #### Navbar                                                                                                                                       
   
  - Fixed link clipping — nav links now render fully at all viewport widths (`navbar-links` no longer competes with `navbar-spacer` for flex space) 
  - Removed the placeholder "Service Mapping — soon" item                                                                                         

  ---

  ### Developer Experience

  #### Report Issue Button

  - Amber-styled button with an animated pulse dot and EKG-line icon, positioned left of the AI Assistant button                                    
  - Links directly to the GitHub Issues page at `karastoyanov/sn-explorer/issues`
  - Hidden on mobile alongside the AI Assistant button                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                  
  #### GitHub Issue Templates

  Three structured templates added under `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`:                                                                                 
   
  | Template | Label | Key fields |                                                                                                                 
  |---|---|---|                                                                                                                                   
  | `bug_report.yml` | `bug` | What happened, steps to reproduce, affected section, environment |
  | `data_issue.yml` | `data` | Affected section, what is wrong, correct value or reference |
  | `feature_request.yml` | `enhancement` | Feature description, problem it solves, area of the app |                                               
   
  ---

releases.name: v1.0.0
releases.body:
## v1.0.0 — 2026-06-03

First public release of **SN Discovery Explorer** — a local web application for browsing and querying ServiceNow Discovery configuration synced from a live instance.

### What's included

**Pattern & Classifier Browser**
- Browse all Discovery patterns with filtering by category and discovery type
- View full pattern detail: NDL steps, CI mappings, relations, prepost scripts, extension sections, trigger rules, and launch parameters
- Browse all Discovery classifiers with their matching criteria
- Detail pages for Discovery stages and the IRE (Identification & Reconciliation Engine)
**ServiceNow Sync Scripts**
- `extract_patterns.py` — pulls all patterns from a live instance via REST API into a self-contained JSON file; supports active-only filtering, targeted extraction by sys_id, parallel fetch workers, and scope limiting
- `extract_classifiers.py` — pulls all classifiers and their classification criteria
- Password can be passed via `--password` flag, `$SNOW_PASSWORD` environment variable, or interactive prompt

**AI Discovery Assistant**
- Conversational chat panel grounded exclusively in your synced data — never uses general training knowledge
- Local RAG pipeline: hybrid BM25 + semantic search (`all-MiniLM-L6-v2`) with Reciprocal Rank Fusion merges keyword precision with semantic understanding
- Context includes full pattern NDL detail (steps, operations, relations, CMDB tables written) enabling questions like "which step maps attributes to the main CI" or "what relations does this pattern create"
- Conversation-aware retrieval — follow-up questions stay anchored to the topic across multiple turns
- OpenAI API key stored in browser `sessionStorage` only — never sent to the backend

**Other**
- Dark / light theme
- Module registry architecture — extensible for Service Mapping and other ITOM modules
